text:
irene: heads up — observed 30–40s stalls on 3 GPU attach requests in us-west2a around 03:12 UTC, looks correlated with local-ssd scrub starting at the same time. logs attached below.
aj: can you paste the log snippet?
irene: dropping a small snippet from the node (sanitized) — looks like the cleaner kicked off and saturated io: 
```log
[2026-03-19T03:12:01Z] cleaner: start scrub device=/dev/nvme1n1 pool=local-attached-0
[2026-03-19T03:12:02Z] io_latency_ms: write=5120 read=1200 path=/var/lib/containerd/io
[2026-03-19T03:12:03Z] gpu-provision: attach request id=gpu-101 state=waiting wait_s=32
[2026-03-19T03:12:04Z] cleaner: parallelism=8 -> scanning hotstripe
```
leo: that parallelism is high for hot nodes. do we still run the scrub window at 03:00 globally?
kai: yes, we have a stagger but the fanout collapsed — several regions drifted into the same minute after DST/cron drift.
ops: saw the same signature last week in us-west2a — replica imbalance+cleaner fanout causes an iops spike that blocks attach paths.
irene: impact: 3 GPU jobs delayed (~1.5m extra provisioning time) + one failed create that retried, cost blip and slightly missed internal SLO.
aj: short-term mitigations: throttle cleaner parallelism on nodes with active attach requests, and add IO niceness (ionice) for scrub process. medium-term: smarter scheduling to avoid scrub during attach windows.
maria: +1 on ionice. also we should consider opportunistic backoff when kubelet reports pending GPU pods.
leo: I'll open a config PR to reduce default parallelism from 8 -> 2 on nodes with >80% GPU attach rate, and add a flag to opt-in ionice. tagging @sre-bot for automated rollout.
sre-bot: queued: deploy config-change #4523 -> canary 5 nodes in us-west2a at 03:50 UTC. monitor: scrub_io_ms, gpu_attach_wait_s. :eyes:
ops: operational ask — add an alert: scrub_io_p95 > 3000ms AND gpu_attach_wait_p50 > 10s in same 5m window. That should catch regressions.
aj: will add the alert + dashboard tile. also rolling back the 03:00 cron to a staggered window across AZs should be quick.
kai: i'll validate history to ensure we don't move to 03:30 and collide with other jobs (backup, telemetry).
irene: immediate action items:
- leo -> PR to change parallelism + ionice flag (owner)
- aj -> create alert & dash (owner)
- kai -> run a 10-node canary today with updated cron spacing (owner)
- ops -> track cost bump for the delayed jobs and mark SLO impact (owner)
Thanks all :raised_hands: let's aim for the canary before EOD PST.
aj: I'll post the alert link here once created.
leo: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cleaner-config/pull/108 — notes in the diff.
ops: will watch the canary and escalate if we see >5% attach failures.
irene: great. if the canary looks good we can roll config to another 20 nodes and monitor.
maria: also consider a small UX change: surface short delays as a brief toast so consumers don't auto-retry immediately. low friction but can avoid double-cost.
leo: agreed, filing a tiny frontend ticket.
sre-bot: canary started on 5 nodes at 03:50 UTC — monitoring targets green so far.
irene: closing loop — initial canary looks fine, attach latency improved ~60% on patched nodes. will follow up with a short postmortem tomorrow.
